Det, der vakte den livligste interesse, var dog ting, som slet ingen forbindelse havde med slaget. Det var, som om disse mænd var så udslidte på sjælen, at de fandt lindring i det mest dagligdags. before: With each fresh blow, the chances of survival for those still standing grew slimmer. The regiment stood in battalion columns three hundred paces apart, but all the men shared the same mood — taciturn and somber. Talk was rare in the ranks and ceased altogether each time the thud of a successful hit was heard with the cry "Stretchers!" Most of the time, on their officers' orders, the men sat on the ground. One, having removed his cap, carefully adjusted and tightened its lining; another rubbed dry clay between his palms to polish his bayonet; another fingered his belt strap and tugged at its buckle; another smoothed and refolded his leg wrappings and put his boots back on. Some built little houses from clods of plowed earth, or braided baskets from the straw in the field. All seemed entirely absorbed in these tasks. When men were killed or wounded, when rows of stretchers passed, or when great masses of the enemy came into view through the smoke, no one paid any attention.
